attacker_pocs.name: empty_enum_tag
attacker_pocs.cmd: cc -fsanitize=address -fno-omit-frame-pointer -g -O1 -I src -I build-asan/src pocs/residual.c -L build-asan -Wl,-rpath,/work/build-asan -lmatio -o /tmp/matio-enum-residual && ASAN_OPTIONS=detect_leaks=0 /tmp/matio-enum-residual
attacker_pocs.why: A MAT5 struct written through the public API contains a zero-element uint32 EnumerationInstanceTag field. Mat_VarReadNext allocates a non-null one-byte zero-size block for its data and calls IsEnumStruct. The shipped check tests the element width, which remains four bytes, then reads four bytes from that block. The upstream fix tests nbytes and returns before the read.

role_a_rationale: The commit replaces the missing size check with a check of data_size, which plausibly validates the uint32 element type but does not establish that any element is stored. Ordinary nonempty enum tags retain a four-byte element size and the existing comparison. An empty uint32 tag reaches the same four-byte out-of-bounds read, while the upstream nbytes guard rejects it.
